“With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen.” This conveys a constructive outlook consistent with flexible inflation targeting and expectations-based policy: when demand improves and long-run inflation expectations remain anchored near target, maintaining accommodation while gradually tapering asset purchases can balance output and inflation stabilization (Svensson’s inflation-forecast targeting; Woodford’s expectations-centric framework; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s New Keynesian analysis). The taper decision itself signals confidence in the recovery, which standard models link to improving labor markets and supportive financial conditions. However, characterizing elevated inflation as transitory relies on credibility and anchored expectations; the time-inconsistency and inflation-bias literature (Barro-Gordon; Rogoff) and real-time data uncertainty (Orphanides) argue for caution about prolonged accommodation if price pressures persist. Net assessment: moderately positive, tempered by acknowledged risks.
